analysis:
The PR removes the retained console-ui lint/build job and its `console` output from CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml route lane and lint-console job; component-changes.yml outputs). It also updates AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md to drop the retained console snapshot references. The change is CI scope reduction and documentation, with no provider runtime, protocol, attestation, encryption, cache or fan-helper code touched. Threat IDs T-041, TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-010, TB-011 and TB-012 are not affected.

CI posture: top-level permissions remain `contents: read`, actions stay pinned to SHAs, and the route job keeps `permissions: {}`. The provider-test-gate still requires the provider lanes to match the classifier result. Removing the console output from component-changes.yml does not break the gate, because `provider-test-gate` only reads `needs.changes.outputs.provider`. No new secrets, triggers (e.g. pull_request_target) or untrusted-input interpolation into shell are introduced. Existing `${{ }}` use is limited to env vars or controlled values.

Unverified contracts: scripts/ci-component-paths.py still might emit `console=` to GITHUB_OUTPUT. This is harmless, but I could not see that file. Also, scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py and test-darkbloom-route.py in release-integrity might still expect a lint-console lane, which would be a CI breakage and not a security issue. Removing the console build/lint is a loss of CI coverage only for the retained console-ui snapshot, which the threat model scopes out (backend and console are out of scope). The docs state that console development is platform-owned. Nothing here weakens a provider-side control.

No findings. Remaining integration question: whether the helper scripts and the Makefile, which are outside this batch, were updated consistently. That is a correctness matter, not a security one.
